entries.title: Search displaces email
entries.quote: Consumers may well change their use of the Internet, with search potentially displacing email as the most used digital application.
entries.subject: Web search
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the executive summary of the Technology report. Section title is Hindsight's label; the report's section headings were not read.

entries.title: Digital data volume
entries.quote: it is forecast that approximately 20 exabytes (billion gigabytes) of new digital data will be created in 2006.
entries.subject: Digital data growth
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the executive summary of the Technology report. 'it is forecast' may cite an outside forecast.

entries.title: R&D collaboration and offshoring
entries.quote: With global R&D spending expected to top $1 trillion in 2006, companies will be increasingly likely to seek to share their R&D burden with others.
entries.subject: R&D collaboration
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the executive summary of the Technology report.

entries.title: Internet regulation
entries.quote: Some governments may move to tax Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) services in the same manner as traditional Public Switched telephone Network (PSTN)
entries.subject: Internet regulation (VoIP tax)
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the executive summary of the Technology report.

entries.title: Open source
entries.quote: The software world will likely see its dynamics continue to change, as open source becomes a growing threat to the established software business model
entries.subject: Open source software
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the executive summary of the Technology report.

notes: 5th edition by count from 2002. Series title 'TMT Trends: Predictions, 2006', published as separate Technology, Media and Telecommunications reports. Only the executive summary of the Technology report was read (Mondaq). Entries are summary-level statements, not the report's headline predictions; labels are Hindsight's.
